items.title: U.S. Equity Market Outlook: It Takes a Village
items.summary: The S&P 500 is touching new highs. We've been consistently of the view that the path to our year-end 8100 base-case target will require both the AI-influenced and more macro-impacted halves of the market to participate. A quick look at cluster performance helps show how this would happen.

items.title: North America Internet: The Muse Moment
items.summary: We think Muse could generate more than $27 billion in revenue at scale, reshaping how we search and shop as personal agents become always-on habits. We include thoughts from equity analysts about potential impacts on sectors ranging from AI and semis to homebuilders and utilities.

items.title: U.S. Semiconductors: The Implications of Personal Agents
items.summary: Given recent personal-agent launches, we now estimate 2030's CPU total addressable market at $300 billion. Always-on agents will significantly increase inference-related compute, memory and networking consumption. We raise our target price for AMD to $800 as a primary beneficiary.

items.title: U.S. Airlines: Third-Quarter Preview
items.summary: As we approach earnings season for U.S. airlines, we're upgrading JBLU to Neutral/High Risk given its significant share-price decline since our August downgrade to Sell/High Risk. We're also issuing a positive catalyst watch on ALGT. We offer further analysis and revisions in this note.

items.title: U.S. Application Software: Bus Tour Takeaways, Day 1
items.summary: We hosted investor meetings with ADBE, ADSK, GWRE, CRM and ZM and found these companies largely consistent in discussing demand patterns, with recurring themes around adapting product/packaging for AI. We offer company-by-company takeaways from these discussions in this note.

items.title: Japan Chemicals: Semi-Materials Markets Look Primed for Growth
items.summary: Japanese firms are highly competitive in semi-materials markets, with hyperscalers looking to ensure stable procurement. As we note in this Deep Dive, volume growth in semi-materials markets could accelerate and supply/demand is tightening, adding to momentum for raising prices.

items.title: Implications of Spain's Snap Elections
items.summary: Spain will hold early elections at the end of November, with polls suggesting a right-of-center alliance led by the conservative PP will take the helm. If so, we'd expect a continuation of Spain's cautious fiscal approach and a pro-European stance. We consider further implications herein.

items.title: Australia Economics: A Plunge in Consumer Sentiment
items.summary: Australian consumer sentiment plunged to 80.4 in October, driven by persistent cost-of-living pressures compounded by rising interest rates. The lone bright spot? Job vacancies rose to a two-year high of 122, consistent with positive employment growth signals from business sentiment.

items.title: Global Equity Quarterly: Resilience or Complacence?
items.summary: Despite many headwinds, global equities have climbed ~12% in 2026 and are near all-time highs. Does this relative calm suggest equity fundamentals will prove resilient, or will a correction eventually be needed to more accurately reflect risk? We remain in the “resilience” camp for now.

items.title: U.S. Midterms on the Mind: Implications Across Assets
items.summary: Consensus sees a House flip, and a Democratic sweep wouldn't surprise us. The outlook looks typical: lower equities and higher yields, USD and energy into the event, with a price reversal afterwards. But there are nuances to consider across equity sectors and regions, as we explore herein.

items.title: QIS Corner: Systematic Strategies and the U.S. Midterms
items.summary: We examine systematic strategies' behavior around U.S. midterm elections, building on our prior efforts. Among commodity QIS strategies, curve and vol carry have historically outperformed post-election, while value-type strategies such as skewness and producer margin have lagged.

items.title: U.S. MedTech: Third-Quarter Preview
items.summary: After a bit of August optimism, MedTech stocks went back to the penalty box in September. Yet while our expectations are low for third-quarter results, we do look for pockets of growth (and recovery) heading into 2027. We review our top picks and offer a quartet of catalyst watches.

items.title: Rate Peak Drives a Rotation in Japanese Equities
items.summary: Long-term rates in Japan have risen to the 3% range, but the market has already priced in rate-hike expectations and fiscal risk. We think a turning point in the market may highlight a shift in funds from banks to real estate and to high-return-on-equity, high-growth stocks.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: The Chase Is on — Adding to Brazil Risk
items.summary: We're adding to our Brazil risk following bullish first-round election results. Flávio Bolsonaro is the more market-friendly candidate, promising fiscal austerity, privatization, deregulation and VAT cuts, with his party's strong Senate showing a good sign for a legislative agenda.

items.title: Brazil Equity Strategy: Election Update
items.summary: First-round election results from Brazil saw Flávio Bolsonaro at ~47% vs. ~45% for Lula, making Bolsonaro the frontrunner heading into the second round. This should be viewed positively by the market given expectations for more market-friendly policies and stronger fiscal discipline.

items.title: MedTech Vs. Tools: A Classic Investor Question
items.summary: Can MedTech work if Life Science Tools is working? Does one need to be out of favor for the other to benefit? We explore this question again with the S&P E&S Index (Medtech) down 20.6% year to date while the S&P LS&T Index (Life Sciences) is up 14.7%, and also review our top picks.

items.title: Artificial Intelligence: Building the Rails for Scaled Intelligence
items.summary: Gemini 4 Argon's design extends the frontier trend of building models for agents tackling multi-step work across ever-larger software projects, while delayed broad availability follows an industry shift toward more time to strengthen safeguards and improve efficiency before monetization.

items.title: Trust Banks: Third-Quarter Earnings Preview
items.summary: Trust banks have outpaced more traditional banks by more than 15% year to date. We continue to think STT offers the best risk/reward at this valuation, but note that given trust banks' gains, operational risk will likely be more punitive on the downside with near-term earnings turbulence.

items.title: Implications of Nike’s Distribution Strategy Pivot, Pt. 5
items.summary: Nike will likely take back a massive scale of channel inventories in China in the next three quarters. We continue to expect Chinese brands such as Anta and Li Ning to gain share from Nike; we're positive on Anta’s possible consolidation of Puma China’s retail/distribution business in '27.

items.title: U.S. Economics Weekly: Main Street Vs. Wall Street
items.summary: We see no signs that pockets of strength are leading to any retightening in the broader economy as wage growth continues to slow. We think policymakers will be increasingly uncomfortable weakening the broader economy further with the labor market not a source of inflationary pressure.

items.title: PULSE Monitor: Pondering Paradigms
items.summary: Traditional stock vs. bond math would seem to favor bonds, but our Fair Value approach implies equities can handle higher bond yields, if only barely. We explore issues in equity markets, including how the fundamental discussion is less about 2026 and 2027 than about 2028 and beyond.

items.title: AI in the Hospital: Save Time Today, Generate Returns Tomorrow
items.summary: We hosted Deepti Pandita, Chief Medical Informatics and Chief AI Officer at UC Irvine Health, for a deep dive into how AI is being used in a substantial hospital system, the outlook for MedTech applications, and an exploration of which tools are likely to find favor.

items.title: Retail Weekend Reading: Understanding Tariff Refunds' Impact
items.summary: The year's first half saw IEEPA refunds of U.S. tariffs, which retailers handled in various ways: reinvesting all, reinvesting some, or ignoring it altogether. Approaches to guidance also varied. Given this confusion, we seek to navigate what’s currently important on the tariff front.

items.title: U.S. Broadcasting: Quantifying the Impact of an MLB Lockout
items.summary: We think the most likely scenario in baseball's labor dispute is the owners and players failing to reach an agreement before the start of next season, though we don’t expect the entire season to be canceled. We explore the financial impact for various sectors and the Atlanta Braves.

items.title: Global Macro Strategy: VAR — Volatility Also Rises
items.summary: The rates selloff had reached a stage where it was getting more worrisome for risky assets as rates volatility (MOVE) rose. MOVE tends to be high after the first hike but then flatlines; that said, we're concerned that the most recent leg in the selloff wasn't driven by Fed repricing.

items.title: European Rates Weekly: What to Do About OATs?
items.summary: Turning the tide for spiraling OAT-Bund spreads may need ECB intervention given France's political vacuum, with such intervention now more likely given contagion risk. Ending hikes is a first step, while stopping QT would halve net supply pressure on EGBs. We offer further analysis herein.

items.title: Emerging Markets Strategy Weekly: Not Out of the Woods Yet
items.summary: We think the real yield story can't be disentangled from the rise in U.S. productivity, a refined-product energy risk premium, the UST's struggle to compete for capital against heavy IG AI issuance, and record foreign equity inflows amid weak private UST demand.

items.title: ROI on AI: The Future of Open Is More Control Than Cost
items.summary: The capability gap between frontier and open-weight models is widening again, and usage economics increasingly favor frontier labs’ model suites. We think the long-term value of open models is the control they enable via customization, deployment flexibility and IP protection.

items.title: European Banks: AI Agents and the Threat to Deposits
items.summary: We continue to see fears about AI agents hurting bank deposits and pricing as overblown, but we do think such worries will change how banks think about the value of relationships vs. tactical deposits. In this note, we discuss which markets we see as at greatest risk from AI adoption.

items.title: The Speculative-Grade Beat: Reading the UST Leaves
items.summary: High-yield spreads finally responded to the relentless rise in Treasury yields, but remain fairly resilient given the volatile backdrop. A difference between the current selloff and prior episodes is that improved growth prospects account for a sizable portion of higher yields.

items.title: U.S. Construction Materials: Earnings Preview
items.summary: We expect a challenging second half for Construction Materials names as diesel prices hit margins, and note that price initiatives are tough to push late in the year. Accordingly, we expect most producers to cut FY ‘26 guides. But we also think a favorable setup may be forming for 2027.

items.title: Home Improvement Insights Summit: Uncertainty Weighs on Growth
items.summary: Our key takeaway from the HIRI Home Improvement Insights Summit: "Uncertainty" is the overhang weighing on 2026 industry growth. Rising energy costs and interest rates, worsening housing affordability and geopolitics have all limited the return to “normal” growth.

items.title: Africa Economics & Strategy Weekly: CEMAC and the IMF
items.summary: We discuss how the three main economies in the Economic and Monetary Community of Central Africa are progressing in their negotiations with the IMF. We also explore Nigeria's monetary-policy path after its central bank opted for an unexpectedly large rate cut in September.

items.title: What Rising U.S. Yields Mean for Latin America's Borrowing Bill
items.summary: We see the recent surge in U.S. long-term yields as a differentiating force across Latin America rather than a uniform headwind, amplifying pre-existing vulnerabilities in higher-debt sovereigns but leaving resilient credits comparatively insulated. We offer further analysis in this note.

items.title: We're Downgrading Moderna to Sell/High Risk
items.summary: We’re downgrading Moderna to Sell/High Risk after an outsized run and amid struggles to justify the valuation through public-company comparisons or pipeline net present value. MRNA’s ~$80 billion market cap approximates Regeneron’s despite materially lower expected revenue and earnings.

items.title: Core PCE Is Revised Even Lower Than Expected
items.summary: Core PCE inflation rose 0.25% month over month and 3.01% year over year in August, softer than we'd expected. While still above target, core PCE is now clearly softer than the latest Fed forecasts, which we think will encourage policymakers to "wait and see" before pursuing further hikes.

items.title: U.S. Lodging and REITs: Impacts of an Agentic AI World
items.summary: We consider the potential impacts of agentic AI on real estate fundamentals, as well as trading/macro considerations given that REITs are generally considered “risk off” vs. the broad market. We offer initial thoughts by sector, while staying humble knowing that the technology is evolving.

items.title: The Shape of Boeing's Free Cash Flow Steepens
items.summary: We're lowering our Boeing free cash flow estimates to account for a steepening ramp over the next several years. As we explore in this note, we expect near-term trading to stay data-driven until we have some degree of resolution on recent certification and labor issues at BA.

items.title: Western Europe Airlines: Legacy Airline Competitive Capacity
items.summary: Our competitive overlap analysis for EU legacy airlines shows another month of broad-based cuts to scheduled capacity. While capacity growth remains lower on legacy carriers' networks vs. low-cost carriers, larger cuts for low-cost names show the gap is narrowing.

items.title: Western Europe Aerospace & Defense: EU Spending Hints
items.summary: The European Council has identified five "European Defence Projects of Common Interest." We offer our analysis of potential implications in this note, including the observation that traditional defense should continue to dominate spending and air defense seems to be the main priority.

items.title: North America Specialty Chemicals: Trimming Coatings Estimates
items.summary: Coatings companies have seen relative weakness in September given higher oil prices, rate hikes and continued weakness in housing, autos and Europe. We trim EPS estimates ~2% for the rest of the year and 2027. We see price/cost expansion as likely significant in next year's second half.

items.title: India Economics: El Niño Risks Are Still Unfolding
items.summary: India's macro risks are rising as the monsoon nears its end, with rainfall deficits in key agricultural states possibly threatening yields. The focus will shift to tracking elevated daily temperatures as heat-wave risks are heightened during the March-April harvest period.
